clue.text: Debauched rag do at uni — students looking forward to it?

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted or led astray, so these letters are thrown out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A rowdy student party at university is the event the undergraduates are eagerly awaiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Students work towards the ceremony at which they receive their degrees, so it is the day they anticipate.

clue.text: Chronic complainer in great cry of pain

parts.note: GR is a standard abbreviation for great
ouch is what you shout when hurt

explanation.surface: A habitual moaner suffering a great deal of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a grumbler, someone who habitually complains about everything.

clue.text: Smoking receptacle hotel's thrown out, or lost

indicators.note: thrown out tells us the hotel is ejected from the receptacle's letters

parts.note: an ashtray holds cigarette ash
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel has got rid of its ashtrays, or perhaps simply mislaid them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off or gone missing, the sense of mislaid.

clue.text: Touring America, club singer one performing incognito?

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the rearranged letters go around the letter for America
performing suggests the words putting on a show in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nightclub singer on an American tour plays the show under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CLUB SINGER ONE are rearranged and 'Touring' wraps them around A for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito is in disguise, so they cannot be identified by anyone who sees them.

clue.text: Insect one bug found in baby hospital?

indicators.note: found in tells us the one and the bug are discovered inside the baby

parts.note: a tot is a small child
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bug can be a germ, as in a stomach bug
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor finds an insect, or a germ, on a newborn in a maternity ward.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger moth is a family of brightly patterned moths, and every moth is an example of an insect.

clue.text: Last symbol of resistance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of anything
second meaning: the capital form of this Greek letter is the sign for the ohm, the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a final emblem of political rebellion; in fact resistance is the electrical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'alpha and omega' the Greek letter stands for the end, and physicists write the ohm with the same letter.

clue.text: Where you may see Victoria and Mike crawl?

parts.note: London Victoria station is in the SW1 postcode district, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where one might spot Victoria and Mike creeping along.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postcode around Victoria station, here written with I for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, crawl can mean to move through water using the front-crawl stroke.

clue.text: Cattle-herder with park official crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the park official stretches across and around the line

parts.note: a ranger patrols a national park

explanation.surface: A cowhand and a park warden cross a line together.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West a wrangler is a cowboy who looks after horses or livestock.

clue.text: Sensible friend on Oder's banks

indicators.note: the friend sits on both banks of the river, so its letters flank the river's name

parts.note: mate is a British word for friend
the Oder is a river between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A level-headed companion stands by the banks of the river Oder.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate views are reasonable and avoid extremes, which is what a sensible person holds.

clue.text: Neat trio playing in pub with beer and song

indicators.note: in places the rearranged trio inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: playing suggests the words performing in a new arrangement

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A tidy three-piece band performs in a pub over a pint and a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub with beer' reads like a pint at the bar, but each is a separate piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Internationale is the socialist anthem, a famous rallying song of the left.

clue.text: Playful animal more sexy for Cockneys?

indicators.note: Cockneys, Londoners of the East End, famously drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: hotter is slang for more sexy

explanation.surface: An East Londoner describing a frisky creature as rather sexier.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a traditional working-class East Londoner, whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: These river mammals are known for sliding down banks and juggling pebbles, a classic frolicking creature.

clue.text: Callow youth taking in new country

parts.note: green means inexperienced or callow

indicators.note: taking in means the youth absorbs the letter for new

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young man is shown around an unfamiliar land.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenland is a vast Arctic island, an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

clue.text: Husband occupying house an opportunist

indicators.note: occupying means the husband lives inside the house

parts.note: Cancer is one of the twelve houses or signs of the zodiac
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A husband moves into a house, an opportunist out for what he can get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a dwelling, but astrology calls each zodiac sign a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer, British informal, is someone who takes risks or exploits any opening for gain.

clue.text: One to settle scores opposing Spain in rage

indicators.note: in places the opposing and Spain letters inside the rage

parts.note: anger is rage
V for versus means against or opposing
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Someone out for revenge, furious and set against Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger takes revenge for a wrong, getting even with whoever caused it.

clue.text: This attained, so: can one get involved, cuddling female?

indicators.note: cuddling means the rearranged letters wrap around the letter for female
involved means twisted or entangled, so the words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Once a certain age is reached, may someone then get involved and embrace a woman?
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SO CAN ONE GET, and 'cuddling' places F within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a person reaches the legal minimum age for sexual activity, that threshold is attained and the question is answered.

clue.text: Person blending in tea with energy-packed fruit?

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

indicators.note: energy-packed means the fruit is stuffed with the energy letter

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone at a gathering has tea alongside a high-energy fruit snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard changes colour to match its surroundings, so a person who adapts to fit any group is so called.

clue.text: Seafood demand beset by concessions

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the concessions enclose the demand

parts.note: sops are small concessions made to placate someone
a call is a demand, as in a call for action

explanation.surface: A seafood order besieged by placatory compromises.
explanation.definitionFit: These bivalve shellfish are served as a delicacy, a typical item of fish restaurant fare.

clue.text: Charming qualities masking your compiler's ugly looks?

indicators.note: masking means hiding, so the charming qualities conceal the compiler inside

parts.note: graces are charming or elegant qualities
the setter refers to themself; your compiler is = I am, contracted to I'M

explanation.surface: The setter's charm hides how unattractive the setter's face is.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of pain or disgust, an unattractive look.

clue.text: I'm surprised: is brown sauce put into horrible local dish?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: put into means these pieces go inside the horrible

parts.note: nasty means horrible
HP Sauce is the best-known British brown sauce

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to see brown sauce poured on a horrible regional meal.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a tangy brown condiment popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This filled pastry is a traditional speciality of Cornwall, so it is a regional food.

clue.text: One's capacity for it?

parts.note: 'it' is a coy word for sex, so one's capacity for it is the sex drive

explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like a pronoun needing an antecedent; it is the euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The libido is sexual desire or drive, the appetite a person has for sex.

clue.text: What zombie does? Unmentionable things!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a zombie reverses dying
second meaning: underwear, jokingly called unmentionables

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word into UN and DIES, a playful verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is an informal word for underwear, often coyly called unmentionables.

clue.text: Letter in Greek about a dance

indicators.note: about means around, so the Greek letter goes around the a

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek character describing a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance popular around 1990.

clue.text: In sea was Hesperus flooded?

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Was the ship Hesperus swamped at sea?
explanation.walkthrough: The Wreck of the Hesperus is a Longfellow poem about a ship lost in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered with water, as a deck swamped by waves.

clue.text: James Bond for one recalled mark given by Scotsman

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the mark's letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a note is a mark, as in take note
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Bond remembered a grade awarded by a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school; in Fleming's novels Bond attended it before being expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton College, and the fictional spy was one, so he is an example.

clue.text: Seesaw in local site vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: The seesaw in the neighbourhood playground has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, seesaw means to move back and forth repeatedly, swinging between two positions.

clue.text: Defence from boxer swinging both ways?

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
bi is slang for bisexual, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: A boxer's guard as he swings punches left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere when a crime happened, used as a legal plea.

clue.text: Indifferent over after spinner on song initially

indicators.note: after means the over letter comes behind the initials
initially means take the opening letter of each of these words

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cricket over is unremarkable once the spin bowler starts singing.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner is a spin bowler in cricket, which makes 'over' look like a cricket term too.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so describes something mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Below zero inside so like stormy weather?

indicators.note: inside places the below and zero letters within the so

parts.note: thus means so, therefore
under means below
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: Freezing temperatures below zero, so stormy weather follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderous describes loud rumbling like thunder, a feature of stormy weather.
